intended_object: The d-th coordinate projection from affine D-space 𝔸^D_K = Spec K[X_d : d ∈ D] to the additive group scheme 𝔾_a = Spec K[t], as a morphism of schemes over Spec K. It is given on rings by t ↦ X_d. This is inferred from the docstring, the name, and its use as the legs of the product fan `additiveGroupAffineProductFan`.
explanation:
The body applies `algSpec K`, which is Spec on K-algebras landing in schemes over Spec K, to a K-algebra map `additiveProductCoordinateAlgHom K D d`. That map goes from the coordinate ring of 𝔾_a, `SymmetricAlgebra K K` ≅ K[t], to `MvPolynomial D K`. It is the lift of the K-linear map K → K[X] given by 1 ↦ X_d, so it sends the generator t to X_d, as the simp lemma `additiveProductCoordinateAlgHom_coordinate` confirms. Spec of this ring map is exactly the d-th coordinate projection 𝔸^D_K → 𝔸^1_K = 𝔾_a. Because it is built through `algSpec`, it is automatically a morphism over Spec K. The library goes on to prove that these projections make Spec K[X_D] the categorical product of copies of 𝔾_a over Spec K, which confirms they are the right maps.

The generality is natural: K is any commutative ring. The section variable `[Fintype D]` is included automatically but not used here; the projection would make sense for any index type D. Finiteness is the setting of the whole module, which compares with the finite product of group objects (∏ᶜ in Grp), and that comparison does need finite D. This is a minor carried-over hypothesis on an auxiliary component, not a real narrowing of a standard notion. Mathlib has no direct counterpart into this model of 𝔾_a. The closest is `AffineSpace.reindex`, applied to a map Unit → D, but it lands in 𝔸(Unit; S) rather than in Spec of the symmetric algebra.
